external_contracts: ERR queue state is per-thread; ERR_get_state's pointer is valid until thread exit and must not cross threads.

Pointers returned by ERR_get/peek/error_string point into the ring or static storage and are valid only until the next queue mutation or, for the static buffer, the next ERR_error_string(NULL) call on any thread.
ERR_error_string(NULL) is not thread-safe and requires external synchronization (authority parity).
ERR_set_error_data transfers ownership only with ERR_TXT_MALLOCED; without it the pointer stays borrowed.
OSSL_ERR_STATE_save/save_to_mark/restore require states from OSSL_ERR_STATE_new (or an equivalent state satisfying the slot contract), never the thread's own state.
Allocator hooks installed by CRYPTO_set_mem_functions must be valid for the process lifetime and must not re-enter ERR on the same thread (retained; see NEO-ERR-7).
strerror_r is the GNU variant (glibc); the XSI variant has a different ABI.

allocator_hook_reentrancy.edge: with_state holds &mut ErrState while slot_buf_alloc/OwnedStr::adopt run, so an installed CRYPTO_set_mem_functions hook runs with that reference live.
allocator_hook_reentrancy.reachability: Only an application-installed allocator hook that calls an ERR entry point on the same thread. No in-crate caller does this.
allocator_hook_reentrancy.current_status: Documented as outside the contract in err.rs:823-831, but CRYPTO_set_mem_functions' # Safety (mem.rs:907-916) does not state it.
allocator_hook_reentrancy.risk: A re-entrant hook creates a second &mut to the same ErrState: Rust UB. The authority has the same recursion hazard but not a Rust aliasing violation.
allocator_hook_reentrancy.required_resolution: Either state the non-reentrancy external contract at CRYPTO_set_mem_functions (and accept it in the discharge review), or add a thread-local reentrancy guard that makes the nested call return None. A guard is the stronger resolution and is recommended before DISCHARGE.

residuals.text: The thread-local ErrState has no Drop; owned data buffers in the TLS queue are not released at thread exit. This is authority-parity by design and is a resource residual, not UB. Miri's leak checker observes it.
with_state reaches the shared per-thread state through dso_shared::err_state_ptr, so both DSOs observe the authority binding's one queue.
Pointers returned by get/peek and error_string point into the ring/static storage and are valid only until the next queue mutation; authority parity.
ERR_add_error_txt does not implement the authority's ERR_PRINT_BUF_SIZE-100 split; only manifests for ~4 KiB error data; no court probes it.
ERR_load_strings/_const/_unload are no-ops returning 1, so provider-supplied strings are not registered.
Error-queue text is PUBLIC_DATA metadata and is not cleansed; the authority does not cleanse it either.

guard_ffi catches unwinding but uses AssertUnwindSafe; it does not repair arbitrary partial state. For ERR's own slots an interrupted raise is invisible (err_buffer 0), so the local mutation is failure-atomic.
strerror_r is assumed to be the GNU variant; the XSI variant has an incompatible ABI.

The C borrowed-data probe is a court source under courts/phase4 and is not part of `cargo test`; it is built manually against target/debug/libopenssl_rs.a. The Rust unit test covers the ownership decision but not the C adapter's own branch.

NEO-ERR-6 is repaired at the entry points: CRYPTO_malloc, CRYPTO_zalloc, CRYPTO_calloc and CRYPTO_malloc_array are now `pub unsafe extern "C" fn` with a NULL-or-NUL-terminated `file` contract; symbols, signatures and the C ABI are unchanged. 247 in-crate call sites were updated. 24 of those sites forward a private owner-constructor parameter `file: *const c_char` and are recorded as retained caller obligations of those owners (they pass static coordinates today); converting them to SeamFile is a separate owner-model sweep.

newly_exposed_obligations.finding: openssl_rs_err_take_data detaches the slot pointer without reporting whether it was ERR_TXT_MALLOCED. err_variadic.c then unconditionally CRYPTO_reallocs the result. If a slot holds borrowed data (ERR_set_error_data(data, flags without MALLOCED)) and ERR_set_error/ERR_vset_error follows on the same slot, a caller-owned pointer is passed to CRYPTO_realloc: invalid free/realloc and UB.
newly_exposed_obligations.reachable_by: external C ABI; not imported by pure-ftpd
newly_exposed_obligations.required: Either (a) state and enforce that take_data may only be called on a MALLOCED slot and make the adapter fail closed otherwise, or (b) have take_data copy borrowed data into a fresh seam block (or return NULL) before detaching. Then document the returned ownership/extent in # Safety.
newly_exposed_obligations.repair: option (b): take_data now always returns NULL or one whole seam block. A MALLOCED slot transfers ownership; a borrowed slot is copied into a fresh slot_buf_alloc(p_size) block and the borrowed original is left untouched. The helper signature and the C ABI are unchanged. # Safety/ownership text and the adapter comment state the invariant.
newly_exposed_obligations.proof: courts/phase4/rt_err_borrowed_data_probe.c runs ERR_new -> ERR_set_debug -> ERR_set_error_data(static borrowed, flags=0) -> ERR_set_error(fmt) through the real C variadic adapter: data=[raised: ok], flags=3, borrowed unchanged, RC=0, under both plain build and GCC ASan. Rust unit test take_data_copies_borrowed_data_before_the_adapter_reallocs reproduces the adapter's exact grow-to-1024/shrink realloc sequence on the returned block and asserts taken != borrowed.
newly_exposed_obligations.negative_control: probe --negative hands the borrowed static pointer to CRYPTO_realloc (the pre-fix shape): plain build aborts with 'realloc(): invalid pointer' (RC=134); ASan reports 'attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed' / bad-free at CRYPTO_realloc. The env-gated Rust test borrowed_realloc_negative_control_fires_only_when_enabled produces the same ASan bad-free with OPENSSL_RS_ERR_NEGATIVE_CONTROL=1.
newly_exposed_obligations.remaining: independent reviewer must re-derive the invariant and accept that no other caller of take_data exists (only err_variadic.c).

newly_exposed_obligations.finding: openssl_rs_err_finish_data stores the caller's size without requiring it to be consistent with the owned block. OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore later copies err_data_size bytes from that slot, so a size larger than the allocation becomes an out-of-bounds read.
newly_exposed_obligations.reachable_by: external C ABI plus OSSL_ERR_STATE_save/restore; not imported by pure-ftpd
newly_exposed_obligations.required: With MALLOCED and non-NULL data: size >= 1, size <= allocation extent, and a NUL within size. State this in # Safety.
newly_exposed_obligations.repair: finish_data's # Safety now states the size >= 1, size <= extent and NUL-within-size preconditions and why restore makes them load-bearing. The zero-extent MALLOCED case is enforced at runtime: the block is released through the seam and the slot stores no data instead of recording an extent that a later size-driven copy would trust.
newly_exposed_obligations.proof: unit test finish_data_rejects_a_zero_extent_malloced_block allocates a 4-byte seam block, calls finish_data with size 0, and observes reason 42 with flags 0 and no stored data; Miri (SB/TB) and ASan see the release with no leak/UB.
newly_exposed_obligations.remaining: an overstated non-zero size (size > extent) cannot be detected without allocator introspection; it remains a caller contract and an independent reviewer must decide whether the external ABI can supply it.

newly_exposed_obligations.finding: OSSL_ERR_STATE_save/save_to_mark call dst.clear_all(true)/clear(i, true), which frees any slot whose MALLOCED flag is set. The # Safety text does not require the destination's MALLOCED slots to be seam blocks exclusively owned by the destination.
newly_exposed_obligations.reachable_by: external C ABI; not imported by pure-ftpd
newly_exposed_obligations.required: Require es to be a state from OSSL_ERR_STATE_new (or every MALLOCED slot to satisfy the slot contract), exclusively owned and not the calling thread's state.
newly_exposed_obligations.repair: Both save and save_to_mark now state the destination ownership/provenance contract: OSSL_ERR_STATE_new, or every MALLOCED slot is one whole seam block exclusively owned by es and unreleased; es is exclusively owned and not mutated concurrently.
newly_exposed_obligations.proof: No runtime provenance marker exists in the public #[repr(C)] ERR_STATE layout, so destination provenance cannot be cheaply validated without changing the ABI. Documentation alone is not discharge under AGENTS.md section 7.
newly_exposed_obligations.remaining: independent reviewer must either accept the external contract or require an ABI-compatible provenance tag; no positive control exists for a valid destination beyond the existing save/restore tests.

newly_exposed_obligations.finding: OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore copies err_data_size bytes from err_data and duplicates err_file/err_func as C strings. The # Safety text says only 'live state owned by the caller', omitting the per-slot extent, NUL-termination and no-concurrent-mutation requirements.
newly_exposed_obligations.reachable_by: external C ABI; not imported by pure-ftpd
newly_exposed_obligations.required: State: non-NULL err_data is readable for err_data_size bytes; err_file/err_func are NULL or NUL-terminated; es is not mutated concurrently and is not the thread's own state.
newly_exposed_obligations.repair: restore's # Safety states the source extent, NUL termination and no-concurrent-mutation requirements. A cheap authority-compatible check was added: top/bottom outside 0..ERR_STATE_SLOTS are treated as an empty state instead of indexing out of bounds or walking the ring forever. err_data_size remains trusted as the extent because bounded copying would change authority behaviour and no provenance metadata is available.
newly_exposed_obligations.proof: New unit test restore_rejects_an_out_of_range_ring_instead_of_walking_forever writes top = ERR_STATE_SLOTS + 7 and observes a clean return and free; it passes under Miri SB/TB, ASan and TSan.
newly_exposed_obligations.remaining: independent reviewer must accept the external source contract or require a bounded-copy design.

newly_exposed_obligations.finding: ERR_error_string(e, NULL) writes the process-global 256-byte buffer. The prose documented that the authority is not thread-safe, but the # Safety section stated only 'buf NULL or writable for at least 256 bytes'. Concurrent calls/reads are a Rust data race and therefore UB.
newly_exposed_obligations.reachable_by: pure-ftpd imports ERR_error_string; classic usage is ERR_error_string(ERR_get_error(), NULL)
newly_exposed_obligations.required: Add to # Safety: with NULL buf the returned pointer aliases a process-global buffer; calls and reads must be externally synchronized, and the pointer is valid only until the next ERR_error_string call on any thread.
newly_exposed_obligations.repair: The # Safety block now states the process-global alias, the mandatory external serialization of calls and reads, and the valid-until-next-call lifetime. The shared static is retained (authority-compatible: pointer identity and overwrite observation are preserved); no thread-local divergence was introduced.
newly_exposed_obligations.proof: error_string_uses_the_authority_format still passes under Miri SB/TB (single-threaded test only); no concurrent-access test is claimed because the contract forbids one.
newly_exposed_obligations.remaining: independent reviewer must confirm the consumer/ABI contract is acceptable for a C caller (pure-ftpd's usage is serialized).

newly_exposed_obligations.finding: CRYPTO_malloc/zalloc/calloc/malloc_array (safe extern C fns) pass their `file` argument to report_alloc_err -> raise_with -> c_strlen on the allocation-failure path, but their API does not require `file` to be NULL or NUL-terminated. A safe Rust caller can pass an arbitrary raw pointer.
newly_exposed_obligations.reachable_by: safe Rust and C callers of the allocator seam; not reached by pure-ftpd's imported ERR symbols
newly_exposed_obligations.required: Document the NULL-or-NUL-terminated precondition on every affected safe extern fn, or stop reading `file` as a string (e.g. copy only from the recorded seam coordinates). Belongs to RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP.
newly_exposed_obligations.disposition: FIXED (entry points are unsafe fns; C ABI unchanged)
newly_exposed_obligations.repair: CRYPTO_malloc, CRYPTO_zalloc, CRYPTO_calloc and CRYPTO_malloc_array are now `pub unsafe extern "C" fn` with a # Safety contract requiring `file` to be NULL or a NUL-terminated C string valid for the call. The internal helpers malloc_request/alloc/dealloc/clear_dealloc/report_alloc_err/raise_integer_overflow are unsafe fns with the same clause, and every other affected entry point (realloc/clear_realloc/free/memdup/strdup/strndup/aligned_alloc) has the clause added to its existing # Safety. C symbols, signatures and the calling convention are unchanged; only Rust callers see the unsafe requirement. 247 in-crate call sites across 143 files were updated with SAFETY-commented blocks.
newly_exposed_obligations.proof: cargo check --lib and cargo check --all-targets pass; the normal library tests (1707) and clippy --all-targets -D warnings pass. The 24 remaining `file` parameter forwards are enumerated in R-ERR-10.
newly_exposed_obligations.remaining: independent reviewer must confirm the ABI and adjudicate the 24 private helper parameters (SeamFile vs an unsafe helper contract).

newly_exposed_obligations.finding: with_state holds &mut ErrState across allocation/release, so an installed allocator hook runs with that reference live. A hook that re-enters an ERR entry point on the same thread creates a second &mut: Rust UB. err.rs documents the hook as outside the contract, but CRYPTO_set_mem_functions' # Safety did not.
newly_exposed_obligations.reachable_by: application-installed allocator hook; not by any in-crate caller
newly_exposed_obligations.required: Either state the non-reentrancy contract at CRYPTO_set_mem_functions and have the discharge reviewer accept it, or add a thread-local reentrancy guard to with_state so nested calls return None. The guard is recommended.
newly_exposed_obligations.repair: err::with_state now acquires a thread-local Cell<bool> guard before touching the state (and before load_crypto_strings). If the slot is already held, it returns None without forming a second &mut; the nested raise is dropped and the outer call completes. The guard is released by Drop on every exit path, including an unwinding closure. No allocator hook or application callback is invoked while the guard is held except through the state operations themselves.
newly_exposed_obligations.proof: New unit test a_reentrant_state_access_is_refused_and_the_guard_resets calls with_state inside with_state, asserts the nested call returns None and the outer call still returns Some, then asserts the guard has reset. Passes under Miri Stacked Borrows and Tree Borrows, ASan and TSan.
newly_exposed_obligations.remaining: A real C allocator-hook reentry harness is not run; the guard is tested directly. Independent reviewer must decide whether that coverage is sufficient or require an instrumented hook.

'remaining_hidden = 0' means nothing found is undisclosed; it does NOT mean the code is safe. B34 repaired NEO-ERR-6 and NEO-ERR-7 in code and added a cheap validation to NEO-ERR-4. NEO-ERR-3 (destination provenance) and NEO-ERR-4 (source extent) remain contract-only because no ABI-compatible runtime check exists, and the 24 private helper parameters noted in R-ERR-10 remain retained caller obligations.
